entries.longDescription: Slots are callable directly or through signal-slot connections.

entries.name: emit
entries.description: Emit a Qt signal.
entries.insertText: emit valueChanged(value);
entries.longDescription: The emit keyword clarifies intent when notifying connected receivers.

entries.name: connect member signal to slot
entries.description: Typed connect between two QObject instances.
entries.insertText:
connect(sender, &SenderType::valueChanged,
        receiver, &ReceiverType::setValue);
entries.longDescription: The modern typed connect syntax is compile-time checked and safer to refactor.

entries.name: connect signal to lambda
entries.description: Handle a Qt signal with a lambda.
entries.longDescription: Very convenient for small UI reactions without adding a dedicated slot method.

entries.name: connect signal to overloaded slot
entries.description: Disambiguate an overloaded slot with qOverload or an explicit cast.
entries.insertText:
connect(spinBox,
        &QSpinBox::valueChanged,
        this,
        qOverload<int>(&MainWidget::setThreshold));
entries.longDescription: When a Qt class exposes overloaded signals or slots, the connect call may need explicit disambiguation. qOverload keeps that syntax readable and type-safe.

entries.name: custom signal from worker to UI
entries.description: Declare a custom signal and deliver data back to the GUI thread.
entries.longDescription: Signals are Qt's primary event-delivery mechanism between components and threads. QueuedConnection is especially important when a worker thread must notify the UI thread safely.

entries.name: installEventFilter object
entries.description: Intercept another object's events with a dedicated filter object.
entries.longDescription: eventFilter is Qt's generic low-level event interception hook. It is useful for keyboard handling, custom shortcuts, drag-and-drop policies, and cross-widget behaviors without subclassing every control.

entries.name: QApplication main
entries.description: Minimal Qt Widgets application entry point.
entries.longDescription: A compact starting point for a Qt Widgets application.

entries.name: QObject-derived widget

entries.longDescription: A common skeleton for custom widgets exposing their own signals and slots.

entries.name: QMainWindow skeleton

entries.longDescription: A practical base for desktop applications with menus, toolbars, and docks.

entries.name: QTimer periodic update

entries.longDescription: QTimer is ideal for UI refresh, polling, and lightweight periodic work inside the event loop.

entries.name: QString formatting

entries.longDescription: QString::arg keeps formatting readable and works well with localized UI text.

entries.name: QVector range loop
entries.description: Iterate over a QVector with range-based for.
entries.longDescription: Qt containers integrate cleanly with modern C++ iteration patterns.

entries.name: eventFilter
entries.description: Intercept events with a Qt event filter.
entries.longDescription: Useful for centralized key, mouse, or focus handling without subclassing every widget.

entries.name: QStandardItemModel setup
entries.description: Populate a table model for a Qt view.
entries.longDescription: A quick way to feed table or tree views before introducing a dedicated model class.

entries.name: custom model skeleton

entries.longDescription: A scalable approach when the view reflects live domain objects rather than ad hoc items.

entries.name: QFile read text
entries.description: Read a text file with QFile and QTextStream.
entries.longDescription: Qt file I/O integrates well with QString and Unicode text.

entries.name: QJsonDocument parse
entries.description: Parse JSON content with Qt.
entries.longDescription: Useful for settings, payload inspection, and lightweight data exchange.

entries.name: QSettings
entries.description: Persist settings with QSettings.
entries.longDescription: QSettings stores user preferences and application state in a cross-platform way.

entries.name: worker object in QThread
entries.description: Move a worker QObject into a dedicated thread.
entries.longDescription: The worker-object pattern is usually safer than putting business logic inside a QThread subclass.

entries.name: QtConcurrent::run
entries.description: Launch background work with QtConcurrent.
entries.longDescription: A lightweight option for one-off tasks when a full worker-object setup is unnecessary.

entries.name: QMutexLocker
entries.description: Guard shared data with QMutexLocker.
entries.longDescription: RAII-style locking reduces the risk of forgetting to unlock the mutex on early returns.

entries.name: QTcpSocket client
entries.description: Connect to a TCP server with QTcpSocket.
entries.longDescription: A straightforward client pattern for tools, diagnostics consoles, and device interfaces.

entries.name: QNetworkAccessManager GET
entries.description: Perform an HTTP GET request in Qt.
entries.longDescription: Useful for REST calls, metadata downloads, or update checks.

entries.name: QLibrary load DLL beside executable
entries.description: Load a runtime library stored next to the Qt executable and report a precise error.
entries.longDescription: Resolve the absolute runtime path from applicationDirPath() when the DLL or shared object is deployed beside the executable. Always log QLibrary::errorString() when loading fails.

entries.name: QLibrary resolve typed C export
entries.description: Resolve an exported C symbol from a dynamically loaded DLL or shared object.
entries.longDescription: QLibrary::resolve() returns a raw symbol pointer. Convert it to a function-pointer type that exactly matches the exported ABI. A C-compatible exported function avoids C++ name mangling.

entries.name: QLibrary validate mandatory symbol table
entries.description: Resolve several mandatory exports and reject an incomplete DLL early.
entries.longDescription: Resolve the complete required API before starting work. This prevents partially initialized applications when one expected DLL symbol is missing or renamed.

entries.name: QLibrary static resolve convenience
entries.description: Resolve one exported symbol without keeping a QLibrary instance explicitly.
entries.longDescription: The static QLibrary::resolve() helper is concise for a single symbol. Use an explicit QLibrary object when you need diagnostics, multiple exports, lifecycle control, or a reusable loader class.

entries.name: Cross-platform shared-library file name
entries.description: Select a runtime shared-library name for Windows, Linux, and macOS.
entries.longDescription: QLibrary is cross-platform, but deployed file names conventionally differ between Windows DLLs, Linux shared objects, and macOS dynamic libraries.

entries.name: QLibrary reusable loader class skeleton
entries.description: Wrap QLibrary and resolved function pointers inside a small reusable loader class.
entries.longDescription: A dedicated loader class centralizes path resolution, exported prototypes, diagnostics, and API validation. Keep the QLibrary object alive while any resolved function pointer may still be used.

entries.name: Export C ABI for QLibrary resolve
entries.description: Export a stable runtime-loadable C function from a Windows DLL or Linux shared object.
entries.longDescription: QLibrary::resolve() works most predictably with a stable C ABI. On Windows export the symbol with __declspec(dllexport); on GCC/Clang builds, explicitly requesting default visibility is useful when hidden visibility is enabled.

entries.name: QLibrary unload lifecycle note
entries.description: Document the lifetime rules for resolved symbols and unloading.
entries.insertText:
/*
 Keep the QLibrary object alive as long as resolved function pointers are used.
 After unload(), every resolved pointer must be considered invalid.
 unload() can fail if another QLibrary instance still references the same library.
 For process-wide driver DLLs, keeping the library loaded until shutdown is often safer.
*/
entries.longDescription: Dynamic-library lifetime bugs are difficult to diagnose. Avoid calling a resolved function after unloading the corresponding library.

entries.name: QLibrary versus QPluginLoader decision
entries.description: Choose between raw exported functions and a Qt plugin object.
entries.longDescription: QLibrary provides explicit runtime symbol resolution. QPluginLoader is intended for Qt plugins and returns a QObject root instance.

entries.name: QPluginLoader interface skeleton
entries.description: Load a Qt plugin DLL and cast its QObject instance to a declared interface.
entries.longDescription: A QPluginLoader-based plugin exports a Qt plugin object rather than individual C symbols. The plugin interface should be declared with Q_DECLARE_INTERFACE and implemented with Q_INTERFACES.

entries.name: CMake Qt Widgets project with runtime DLL
entries.description: Complete Qt Widgets CMakeLists.txt with sources, UI file, dynamic DLL copy, target properties, and installation.
entries.insertText:
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)

project(BLE_Sniffeur VERSION 0.1 LANGUAGES CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

find_package(Qt6 REQUIRED COMPONENTS Widgets)
qt_standard_project_setup()

qt_add_executable(BLE_Sniffeur
    main.cpp
    mainwindow.cpp
    mainwindow.h
    mainwindow.ui
)

target_sources(BLE_Sniffeur PRIVATE
    bledllloader.cpp
    bledllloader.h
    bledevice.h
)

target_link_libraries(BLE_Sniffeur PRIVATE Qt6::Widgets)

set(BLE_DLL_SOURCE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/Scan_BLE_DLL.dll")
if(EXISTS "${BLE_DLL_SOURCE}")
    add_custom_command(TARGET BLE_Sniffeur POST_BUILD
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different
            "${BLE_DLL_SOURCE}"
            "$<TARGET_FILE_DIR:BLE_Sniffeur>/Scan_BLE_DLL.dll"
        COMMENT "Copy Scan_BLE_DLL.dll beside the executable"
    )
else()
    message(WARNING "Scan_BLE_DLL.dll is missing from the project root")
endif()

set_target_properties(BLE_Sniffeur PROPERTIES
    MACOSX_BUNDLE TRUE
    WIN32_EXECUTABLE TRUE
)

include(GNUInstallDirs)
install(TARGETS BLE_Sniffeur
    BUNDLE DESTINATION .
    LIBRARY DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}
    RUNTIME DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR}
)
entries.longDescription: A practical baseline matching a Qt Widgets application that loads a driver DLL dynamically with QLibrary. No import .lib is needed for symbols resolved exclusively at runtime.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)

entries.name: CMake Qt optional modules

find_package(Qt6 REQUIRED COMPONENTS
    Core

    SerialPort
    Concurrent
)

find_package(Qt6 OPTIONAL_COMPONENTS
    Bluetooth
    SerialBus
    WebSockets
    WebChannel
)

target_link_libraries(MyQtApp PRIVATE
    Qt6::Core
    Qt6::Widgets
    Qt6::Network
    Qt6::SerialPort
    Qt6::Concurrent
)

if(TARGET Qt6::Bluetooth)
    target_link_libraries(MyQtApp PRIVATE Qt6::Bluetooth)

entries.name: CMake explicit AUTOMOC AUTOUIC AUTORCC alternative
entries.description: Enable Qt code generation explicitly when not using qt_standard_project_setup().
entries.insertText:
set(CMAKE_AUTOMOC ON)
set(CMAKE_AUTOUIC ON)
set(CMAKE_AUTORCC ON)

add_executable(MyQtApp
    main.cpp
    mainwindow.cpp
    mainwindow.h
    mainwindow.ui
    resources.qrc
)

target_link_libraries(MyQtApp PRIVATE Qt6::Widgets)
entries.longDescription: qt_standard_project_setup() normally enables common Qt CMake defaults. Explicit AUTOUIC, AUTOMOC, and AUTORCC settings remain useful when integrating Qt into an existing CMake project.

entries.name: CMake copy runtime DLL beside executable
entries.description: Copy a dynamically loaded DLL after each successful application build.
entries.insertText:
set(DRIVER_DLL "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/Scan_BLE_DLL.dll")

if(EXISTS "${DRIVER_DLL}")
    add_custom_command(TARGET MyQtApp POST_BUILD
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different
            "${DRIVER_DLL}"
            "$<TARGET_FILE_DIR:MyQtApp>/Scan_BLE_DLL.dll"
        COMMENT "Copy runtime DLL beside MyQtApp"
    )
else()
    message(WARNING "Missing runtime DLL: ${DRIVER_DLL}")
endif()
entries.longDescription: Use POST_BUILD with $<TARGET_FILE_DIR:...> so the runtime DLL is copied next to the produced executable for the active build configuration.

entries.name: CMake cross-platform sidecar shared library
entries.description: Copy a sidecar DLL, SO, or dylib next to the executable according to the target platform.
entries.insertText:
if(WIN32)
    set(DRIVER_FILE "Scan_BLE_DLL.dll")
elseif(APPLE)
    set(DRIVER_FILE "libScan_BLE_DLL.dylib")
else()
    set(DRIVER_FILE "libScan_BLE_DLL.so")
endif()

set(DRIVER_SOURCE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/${DRIVER_FILE}")
if(EXISTS "${DRIVER_SOURCE}")
    add_custom_command(TARGET MyQtApp POST_BUILD
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different
            "${DRIVER_SOURCE}"
            "$<TARGET_FILE_DIR:MyQtApp>/${DRIVER_FILE}"
    )
endif()
entries.longDescription: When the same application is built on several desktop platforms, deploy the conventionally named sidecar shared library for the current target OS.

entries.name: CMake install runtime driver DLL
entries.description: Install a sidecar runtime DLL with the application package.
entries.longDescription: POST_BUILD copying is convenient for development. Add an install(FILES) rule as well when producing an installation tree or package.

entries.name: CMake deploy Qt runtime dependencies
entries.description: Generate an install-time Qt deployment script for a self-contained desktop application directory.
entries.insertText:
include(GNUInstallDirs)

install(TARGETS MyQtApp
    BUNDLE DESTINATION .
    RUNTIME DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR}
)

qt_generate_deploy_app_script(
    TARGET MyQtApp
    OUTPUT_SCRIPT deploy_script
    NO_UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM_ERROR
)

install(SCRIPT ${deploy_script})
entries.longDescription: Qt provides qt_generate_deploy_app_script() for install-time collection of the Qt runtime dependencies required by an application. It is available from Qt 6.3.

entries.name: CMake configure Qt prefix path Windows

cmake --build build --parallel

entries.name: CMake configure build install workflow

entries.name: basic executable project
entries.description: Minimal CMakeLists.txt for an executable.
entries.insertText:
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(MyApp LANGUAGES C CXX)

set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 11)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)

add_executable(MyApp
    src/main.cpp
)
entries.longDescription: A clean starting point for a small application or utility project.

entries.name: shared library + public headers
entries.description: Declare a reusable shared library target.
entries.insertText:
add_library(MyLib SHARED
    src/mylib.cpp
    include/mylib/mylib.h
)

target_include_directories(MyLib
    PUBLIC
        $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
        $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
)
entries.longDescription: This pattern works well when packaging a DLL or shared object with public headers.

entries.name: find_package(OpenCV)
entries.description: Link OpenCV through CMake package discovery.
entries.insertText:
find_package(OpenCV REQUIRED)

target_link_libraries(MyApp PRIVATE ${OpenCV_LIBS})
target_include_directories(MyApp PRIVATE ${OpenCV_INCLUDE_DIRS})
entries.longDescription: A baseline integration pattern for OpenCV-based applications.

entries.name: find_package(Qt6) widgets
entries.description: Link a Qt Widgets application.
entries.insertText:
find_package(Qt6 REQUIRED COMPONENTS Widgets)

target_link_libraries(MyApp PRIVATE Qt6::Widgets)
entries.longDescription: The most common starting point for Qt Widgets desktop applications.

entries.name: generator expressions
entries.description: Set compile definitions by configuration.
entries.insertText:
target_compile_definitions(MyApp PRIVATE
    $<$<CONFIG:Debug>:MYAPP_DEBUG=1>
    $<$<CONFIG:Release>:MYAPP_RELEASE=1>
)
entries.longDescription: Generator expressions help keep configuration-specific logic local to a target.

entries.name: custom command code generation
entries.description: Run a tool before building a target.
entries.insertText:
add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/generated.json
    COMMAND my_generator --out ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/generated.json
    DEPENDS my_generator
    COMMENT "Generating runtime metadata"
)

add_custom_target(generate_metadata DEPENDS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/generated.json)
add_dependencies(MyApp generate_metadata)
entries.longDescription: Useful when headers, resources, or configuration files are generated during the build.

entries.name: install + export
entries.description: Install a library and export CMake package metadata.
entries.insertText:
install(TARGETS MyLib EXPORT MyLibTargets
    RUNTIME DESTINATION bin
    LIBRARY DESTINATION lib
    ARCHIVE DESTINATION lib
)
install(DIRECTORY include/ DESTINATION include)
install(EXPORT MyLibTargets NAMESPACE MyLib:: DESTINATION lib/cmake/MyLib)
entries.longDescription: Important when your project is meant to be reused by other CMake-based projects.

entries.name: gcc compile single C file
entries.description: Compile one C source file into an executable.
entries.insertText: gcc -Wall -Wextra -std=c11 -O2 main.c -o app
entries.longDescription: A compact baseline for command-line C builds with warnings enabled.

entries.name: gcc build multiple sources
entries.description: Compile several C files and include a local include directory.
entries.insertText: gcc -Wall -Wextra -std=c11 -O2 src/main.c src/device.c src/utils.c -Iinclude -o app
entries.longDescription: A common pattern for small and medium C projects before introducing a build system.

entries.name: gcc shared library
entries.description: Build a shared object on Linux with position-independent code.
entries.insertText: gcc -Wall -Wextra -fPIC -shared src/mylib.c -Iinclude -o libmylib.so
entries.longDescription: Useful for plugin systems, reusable modules, and exported C APIs on POSIX targets.

entries.name: gcc debug build
entries.description: Compile with debug information and sanitizers.
entries.insertText: gcc -Wall -Wextra -std=c11 -g3 -O0 -fsanitize=address,undefined main.c -o app
entries.longDescription: A strong default while debugging memory errors, UB, and crashes during development.

entries.name: g++ compile single C++ file
entries.description: Compile one C++ source file into an executable.
entries.insertText: g++ -Wall -Wextra -std=c++20 -O2 main.cpp -o app
entries.longDescription: A straightforward baseline for modern C++ command-line builds.

entries.name: g++ project with include and libs
entries.description: Compile multiple sources and link external libraries.
entries.insertText: g++ -Wall -Wextra -std=c++20 -O2 src/main.cpp src/gui.cpp src/device.cpp -Iinclude -lopencv_core -lopencv_imgproc -o app
entries.longDescription: Useful when a project grows beyond a single source file but you still want a direct command-line build.

entries.name: g++ shared library
entries.description: Build a C++ shared library.
entries.insertText: g++ -Wall -Wextra -std=c++20 -fPIC -shared src/mylib.cpp -Iinclude -o libmylib.so
entries.longDescription: A common starting point for C++ plugins or reusable runtime modules on Linux.

entries.name: g++ debug with sanitizers
entries.description: Compile C++ with debug information and sanitizers.
entries.insertText: g++ -Wall -Wextra -std=c++20 -g3 -O0 -fsanitize=address,undefined main.cpp -o app
entries.longDescription: Very effective while validating ownership, bounds, and lifetime issues in modern C++.

entries.name: MinGW C executable
entries.description: Build a Windows executable with gcc under MinGW.
entries.insertText: gcc -Wall -Wextra -std=c11 src/main.c -Iinclude -o app.exe
entries.longDescription: A practical baseline for small native Windows utilities built with MinGW.

entries.name: MinGW C++ executable
entries.description: Build a Windows C++ executable with g++ under MinGW.
entries.insertText: g++ -Wall -Wextra -std=c++20 src/main.cpp -Iinclude -municode -o app.exe
entries.longDescription: Useful for desktop tools and command-line applications on Windows without MSVC.

entries.name: MinGW DLL build
entries.description: Build a Windows DLL and import library with MinGW.
entries.insertText: g++ -Wall -Wextra -std=c++20 -shared src/mylib.cpp -Iinclude -Wl,--out-implib,libmylib.a -o mylib.dll
entries.longDescription: A common pattern when distributing a DLL together with an import library for MinGW-based clients.

entries.name: windres resource compile
entries.description: Compile a .rc resource file for icons and version info.
entries.insertText:
windres app.rc -O coff -o app_res.o
g++ src/main.cpp app_res.o -o app.exe
entries.longDescription: Useful for Windows icons, version metadata, and manifest embedding.

entries.name: param
entries.description: Parameter block for reusable PowerShell scripts.
entries.insertText:
param(
    [string]$ProjectRoot,
    [switch]$VerboseMode
)
entries.longDescription: A script-level parameter block is the cleanest starting point for reusable PowerShell automation.

entries.name: advanced script skeleton
entries.description: Robust script skeleton with strict mode and error handling.
entries.longDescription: A strong default for build, deployment, and maintenance scripts on Windows.

entries.name: advanced function
entries.description: Reusable PowerShell function with pipeline-friendly parameters.
entries.longDescription: Useful when you want your PowerShell automation to read like a sequence of named operations.

entries.name: ensure directory exists
entries.description: Create a directory only if missing.
entries.longDescription: Very common in build, export, staging, and deployment scripts.

entries.name: copy deployment tree
entries.description: Copy a deployment tree after recreating the destination.
entries.longDescription: A practical pattern for refreshing a deployment folder from build outputs.

entries.name: search files recursively
entries.description: Find files matching a pattern recursively.
entries.insertText:
Get-ChildItem -Path $ProjectRoot -Recurse -Filter *.h |
    Select-Object FullName, Length, LastWriteTime
entries.longDescription: Useful for audits, dependency scans, and bulk processing.

entries.name: replace text in file
entries.description: Read a file, replace text, and write it back.
entries.insertText:
$content = Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath $ConfigFile
$content = $content -replace 'OldValue', 'NewValue'
Set-Content -LiteralPath $ConfigFile -Value $content -Encoding UTF8
entries.longDescription: Handy for templating configs, patching generated files, or updating build metadata.

entries.name: run executable and check exit code
entries.description: Launch a process, wait for completion, and fail on non-zero exit code.
entries.longDescription: The most common pattern for orchestrating external build tools from PowerShell.

entries.name: Start-Process with log redirection
entries.description: Run a process and redirect stdout/stderr to log files.
entries.longDescription: Very useful for tools that produce long logs or that you want to archive after CI/test runs.

entries.name: restart Windows service
entries.description: Restart a Windows service safely.
entries.longDescription: Useful for deployment automation, local agents, and test infrastructure services.

entries.name: read and update JSON
entries.description: Load JSON, update fields, then write it back.
entries.insertText:
$json = Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath $JsonPath | ConvertFrom-Json
$json.version = '1.0.1'
$json.enabled = $true
$json | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $JsonPath -Encoding UTF8
entries.longDescription: A standard pattern for settings files, manifests, and deployment metadata.

entries.name: download file
entries.description: Download a remote file over HTTP or HTTPS.
entries.insertText: Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $Url -OutFile $DestinationFile
entries.longDescription: Useful for dependency bootstrap, installer downloads, or grabbing reference artifacts.

entries.name: CSV import/export
entries.description: Export objects to CSV and read them back.
entries.insertText:
$rows | Export-Csv -Path report.csv -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
$loadedRows = Import-Csv -Path report.csv
entries.longDescription: Good for test reports, bench logs, and human-readable exports.

entries.name: archive release folder
entries.description: Create a ZIP archive from a release directory.
entries.longDescription: A convenient final packaging step before sharing or publishing artifacts.

entries.name: git + build pipeline
entries.description: Pull, configure, build, and package in one script flow.
entries.longDescription: A good baseline when PowerShell becomes your glue layer for the full local workflow.

entries.name: deploy over SCP
entries.description: Push files to a remote Linux machine from PowerShell.
entries.longDescription: Very practical when deploying to Raspberry Pi, Linux targets, or remote test benches.

entries.name: read registry value
entries.description: Read a registry value from HKLM or HKCU.
entries.insertText: $installDir = Get-ItemPropertyValue -Path 'HKLM:SOFTWAREMyCompanyMyTool' -Name 'InstallDir'
entries.longDescription: Useful when integrating with Windows-installed tools and configuration sources.

entries.name: environment variable setup
entries.description: Set a persistent user environment variable.
entries.insertText: [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('MY_TOOL_ROOT', $ToolRoot, 'User')
entries.longDescription: Helpful for developer setup scripts and toolchain bootstrap flows.

entries.name: transcript logging
entries.description: Capture the full script session to a log file.
entries.longDescription: Great when you want a full PowerShell session log for support or diagnostics.

entries.name: declare variable and string interpolation
entries.description: Create variables and interpolate them inside strings.
entries.insertText:
$ProjectRoot = "C:\Work\MyProject"
$BuildType = "Release"
Write-Host "Building $ProjectRoot in $BuildType mode"
entries.longDescription: PowerShell variables start with $. In double-quoted strings, variables are expanded automatically.

entries.name: ${variable} disambiguation
entries.description: Use braces when a variable touches surrounding characters.
entries.insertText:
$name = "tool"
Write-Host "${name}_debug.exe"
Write-Host "Path = ${env:USERPROFILE}\Desktop"
entries.longDescription: ${...} tells PowerShell exactly where the variable name ends. It is especially useful inside strings when text follows immediately after the variable, or when you access scoped variables like ${env:PATH}.

entries.name: array and hashtable
entries.description: Declare an array and a dictionary-like hashtable.
entries.insertText:
$files = @("a.txt", "b.txt", "c.txt")
$settings = @{
    Host = "raspberrypi"
    Port = 22
    Enabled = $true
}
Write-Host $files[0]
Write-Host $settings["Host"]
entries.longDescription: Arrays use @(...). Hashtable literals use @{ key = value }. They are the standard lightweight containers in PowerShell scripts.

entries.name: typed param block
entries.description: Declare a script or function parameter block.
entries.insertText:
param(
    [string]$ProjectRoot,
    [ValidateSet("Debug", "Release")]
    [string]$BuildType = "Release",
    [switch]$Clean
)
entries.longDescription: A param block gives your script a clean public interface with types, defaults, and validation.

entries.name: foreach loop
entries.description: Iterate over a collection with foreach.
entries.longDescription: Use foreach when you want the clearest possible loop over an in-memory collection.

entries.name: for loop with index
entries.description: Classic indexed loop.
entries.longDescription: The PowerShell for loop uses the same three-part structure as C-style languages: init; condition; iteration.

entries.name: while loop
entries.description: Repeat work while a condition remains true.
entries.longDescription: while is useful for polling loops, retry logic, and wait-until-ready script sections.

entries.name: switch pattern
entries.description: Branch on string values with switch.
entries.longDescription: switch is often cleaner than multiple if/elseif blocks when comparing one variable against a set of known values.

entries.name: pipeline with ForEach-Object
entries.description: Transform items coming from the pipeline.
entries.longDescription: ForEach-Object is the pipeline-oriented form of foreach. It is perfect when data is already flowing through the pipeline.

entries.name: launch detached process
entries.description: Start an executable without waiting for it to finish.
entries.insertText: Start-Process -FilePath "myTool.exe" -ArgumentList "--serve", "--port", "9000" -WorkingDirectory $ProjectRoot
entries.longDescription: Without -Wait, Start-Process returns immediately. This is the simplest way to detach a child process from the current script flow.

entries.name: start detached process in new window
entries.description: Spawn a process in its own window style.
entries.insertText: Start-Process -FilePath "cmd.exe" -ArgumentList "/c", "myTool.exe --serve" -WindowStyle Normal
entries.longDescription: Useful when the launched tool should continue living independently, potentially with its own console window.

entries.name: call executable with explicit arguments array
entries.description: Build an argument list safely before launching a native executable.
entries.longDescription: Splatting an array with @arguments is a clean way to avoid fragile string concatenation when calling native tools.

entries.name: @echo off
entries.description: Disable command echo in batch scripts.
entries.insertText: @echo off
entries.longDescription: The usual first line for readable batch scripts.

entries.name: safe batch skeleton
entries.description: Minimal batch script skeleton with local environment.
entries.insertText:
@echo off
setlocal

set "SCRIPT_DIR=%~dp0"
set "PROJECT_ROOT=%SCRIPT_DIR%.."

echo Project root: %PROJECT_ROOT%
entries.longDescription: A practical start for reusable .bat scripts.

entries.name: read arguments
entries.description: Read the first few command-line arguments.
entries.insertText:
@echo off
setlocal

set "MODE=%~1"
set "CONFIG=%~2"

echo MODE=%MODE%
echo CONFIG=%CONFIG%
entries.longDescription: Simple but useful for build wrappers and launcher scripts.

entries.name: if /i config selection
entries.description: Case-insensitive configuration switch.
entries.longDescription: A very common way to maintain a few deployment profiles in one batch file.

entries.name: ensure folder exists
entries.description: Create a directory if it does not exist.
entries.insertText: if not exist "%OUTPUT_DIR%" mkdir "%OUTPUT_DIR%"
entries.longDescription: Useful in build, deploy, and packaging scripts.

entries.name: for /r recursive scan
entries.description: Iterate recursively over matching files.
entries.longDescription: Helpful for deployment audits, packaging steps, and batch processing.

entries.name: robocopy deployment
entries.description: Mirror one directory tree into another.
entries.insertText:
robocopy "%SRC_DIR%" "%DST_DIR%" /MIR /R:2 /W:1
if errorlevel 8 exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%
entries.longDescription: robocopy is usually the safest choice for non-trivial Windows folder deployments.

entries.name: run command and check errorlevel
entries.description: Execute a command and stop on failure.
entries.longDescription: One of the most important batch patterns for reliable automation.

entries.name: start /wait process
entries.description: Launch a process and wait for it to finish.
entries.insertText: start "Build" /wait cmd /c "cmake --build build"
entries.longDescription: Useful when wrapping tools that should remain in their own process window.

entries.name: timestamped log file
entries.description: Append command output to a timestamped log file.
entries.insertText:
set "STAMP=%DATE:~6,4%-%DATE:~3,2%-%DATE:~0,2%_%TIME:~0,2%-%TIME:~3,2%-%TIME:~6,2%"
set "STAMP=%STAMP: =0%"
set "LOG_FILE=build_%STAMP%.log"

cmake --build build > "%LOG_FILE%" 2>&1
entries.longDescription: Good for preserving logs across repeated build and test runs.

entries.name: CMake + MinGW build
entries.description: Configure and build with MinGW from a batch file.
entries.insertText:
@echo off
setlocal

cmake -S . -B build -G "MinGW Makefiles" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
if errorlevel 1 exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%

cmake --build build -j4
if errorlevel 1 exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%
entries.longDescription: A very common pattern for local Windows C/C++ builds under MinGW.

entries.name: gcc compile one C file
entries.description: Compile a single C source file with gcc.
entries.insertText:
gcc -Wall -Wextra -O2 -std=c11 -o app.exe main.c
if errorlevel 1 exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%
entries.longDescription: Useful for tiny utilities, smoke tests, and quick standalone builds.

entries.name: g++ compile one C++ file
entries.description: Compile a single C++ source file with g++.
entries.insertText:
g++ -Wall -Wextra -O2 -std=c++20 -o app.exe main.cpp
if errorlevel 1 exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%
entries.longDescription: A convenient quick-build pattern for examples and experiments.

entries.name: copy DLLs beside exe
entries.description: Copy runtime DLLs into a release folder.
entries.insertText:

import torch
from torch import nn

class SignalCNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_classes: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.features = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv1d(1, 16, kernel_size=7, padding=3),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.MaxPool1d(2),
            nn.Conv1d(16, 32, kernel_size=5, padding=2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool1d(1),
        )
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(32, num_classes)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = self.features(x).squeeze(-1)
        return self.classifier(x)

A = np.array([[0.0, 1.0], [-2.0, -0.5]])
B = np.array([[0.0], [1.0]])
C = np.array([[1.0, 0.0]])
D = np.array([[0.0]])
system = signal.StateSpace(A, B, C, D)
t = np.linspace(0.0, 10.0, 2000)
u = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * 0.5 * t)
t, y, x = signal.lsim(system, U=u, T=t)
entries.longDescription: State-space simulation is the natural representation once systems become multivariable or internally coupled.

import torch
from torch import nn

class SignalClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_classes: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.features = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv1d(1, 16, kernel_size=7, padding=3),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.MaxPool1d(2),
            nn.Conv1d(16, 32, kernel_size=5, padding=2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool1d(1),
        )
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(32, num_classes)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = self.features(x)
        x = x.squeeze(-1)
        return self.classifier(x)

from scipy import signal
import onnxruntime as ort

samples = np.asarray(signal_values, dtype=np.float32)
sos = signal.butter(4, 200.0, btype="lowpass", fs=sample_rate_hz, output="sos")
filtered = signal.sosfiltfilt(sos, samples)
frames = sliding_window_view(filtered, 256)[::128]
window = np.hanning(frames.shape[1]).astype(np.float32)
spectra = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(frames * window[None, :], axis=1)).astype(np.float32)
session = ort.InferenceSession("model.onnx", providers=["CPUExecutionProvider"])
predictions = session.run(None, {session.get_inputs()[0].name: spectra})

image_points = []

objp = np.zeros((pattern_size[0] * pattern_size[1], 3), np.float32)
objp[:, :2] = np.mgrid[0:pattern_size[0], 0:pattern_size[1]].T.reshape(-1, 2)

for path in image_paths:
    image = cv2.imread(path)
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    found, corners = cv2.findChessboardCorners(gray, pattern_size)
    if found:
        object_points.append(objp)
        image_points.append(corners)

ret, camera_matrix, dist_coeffs, rvecs, tvecs = cv2.calibrateCamera(object_points, image_points, gray.shape[::-1], None, None)
entries.longDescription: Camera calibration is fundamental for metric vision, robotics, and distortion correction.

entries.name: transfer function estimate H1
entries.description: Estimate a simple frequency response from cross spectra.

from scipy import signal
import numpy as np

frequencies_hz, Pxy = signal.csd(input_signal, output_signal, fs=sample_rate_hz, nperseg=1024)
_, Pxx = signal.welch(input_signal, fs=sample_rate_hz, nperseg=1024)

H1 = Pxy / Pxx

threshold = sigma * np.sqrt(2.0 * np.log(len(signal_values)))

import sys
import numpy as np
import pyqtgraph as pg
from PySide6.QtCore import QTimer
from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication

app = QApplication(sys.argv)
plot = pg.plot(title="Realtime")
curve = plot.plot(pen="y")

phase = 0.0
def update() -> None:
    global phase
    x = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, 500)
    y = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * 5.0 * x + phase)
    curve.setData(x, y)
    phase += 0.2

timer = QTimer()
timer.timeout.connect(update)
timer.start(50)
plot.show()
raise SystemExit(app.exec())

def worker() -> None:
    time.sleep(1.0)
    messages.put("Done")

def poll_queue() -> None:
    try:
        status.config(text=messages.get_nowait())
    except queue.Empty:
        pass
    root.after(100, poll_queue)

def on_start() -> None:
    status.config(text="Running")
    threading.Thread(target=worker, daemon=True).start()

tk.Button(root, text="Start", command=on_start).pack(padx=8, pady=8)
poll_queue()
root.mainloop()
entries.longDescription: Tkinter widgets should be updated from the GUI thread; a queue plus after() is a safe pattern.

entries.name: QThread worker object
entries.description: Move a worker QObject to a QThread and report results.
entries.insertText:
import sys
from PySide6.QtCore import QObject, QThread, Signal, Slot
from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication, QLabel, QPushButton, QVBoxLayout, QWidget

class Worker(QObject):
    finished = Signal(float)

    @Slot()
    def run(self) -> None:
        result = 42.0
        self.finished.emit(result)

class MainWindow(QWidget):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.label = QLabel("Idle")
        button = QPushButton("Start")
        button.clicked.connect(self.start_worker)
        layout = QVBoxLayout(self)
        layout.addWidget(self.label)
        layout.addWidget(button)
        self.thread: QThread | None = None
        self.worker: Worker | None = None

    def start_worker(self) -> None:
        self.thread = QThread()
        self.worker = Worker()
        self.worker.moveToThread(self.thread)
        self.thread.started.connect(self.worker.run)
        self.worker.finished.connect(self.on_finished)
        self.worker.finished.connect(self.thread.quit)
        self.thread.start()

    def on_finished(self, value: float) -> None:
        self.label.setText(f"Result: {value}")

app = QApplication(sys.argv)
window = MainWindow()
window.show()
raise SystemExit(app.exec())
entries.longDescription: This is the canonical Qt pattern for non-blocking computations from Python GUIs.

entries.insertText:
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from std_msgs.msg import Float32

class SignalPublisher(Node):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__("signal_publisher")
        self.publisher = self.create_publisher(Float32, "signal_level", 10)
        self.timer = self.create_timer(0.1, self.on_timer)
        self.value = 0.0

    def on_timer(self) -> None:
        msg = Float32()
        msg.data = self.value
        self.publisher.publish(msg)
        self.value += 0.1


def main() -> None:
    rclpy.init()
    node = SignalPublisher()
    try:
        rclpy.spin(node)
    finally:
        node.destroy_node()
        rclpy.shutdown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

entries.insertText:
import rclpy
from rclpy.action import ActionClient
from rclpy.node import Node
from example_interfaces.action import Fibonacci

class SequenceClient(Node):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__("sequence_client")
        self.client = ActionClient(self, Fibonacci, "run_sequence")

    def send_goal(self, order: int) -> None:
        goal = Fibonacci.Goal()
        goal.order = order
        self.client.wait_for_server()
        future = self.client.send_goal_async(goal)
        future.add_done_callback(self.on_goal_response)

    def on_goal_response(self, future) -> None:
        goal_handle = future.result()
        if not goal_handle.accepted:
            self.get_logger().warning("Goal rejected")
            return
        result_future = goal_handle.get_result_async()
        result_future.add_done_callback(lambda f: self.get_logger().info(str(f.result().result.sequence)))

from multiprocessing import Process, Queue
import time


def acquire(queue: Queue) -> None:
    for index in range(100):
        queue.put((time.time(), index))
    queue.put(None)


def process(queue: Queue) -> None:
    while True:
        item = queue.get()
        if item is None:
            break
        timestamp, sample = item
        print(timestamp, sample)


queue = Queue(maxsize=1024)
producer = Process(target=acquire, args=(queue,))
consumer = Process(target=process, args=(queue,))
producer.start(); consumer.start()
producer.join(); consumer.join()

import time
from collections import defaultdict

last_seen = defaultdict(lambda: 0.0)
TIMEOUT_S = 2.0


def on_heartbeat(worker_id: str) -> None:
    last_seen[worker_id] = time.monotonic()


def check_timeouts() -> list[str]:

    return [worker_id for worker_id, stamp in last_seen.items() if now - stamp > TIMEOUT_S]

entries.name: volatile flag set by ISR
entries.description: Share a minimal event flag between an interrupt routine and the main loop.
entries.longDescription: A volatile flag is one of the safest first patterns for handing off work from an ISR to non-interrupt code.

entries.name: software debounce
entries.description: Debounce a mechanical button with a time filter.
entries.longDescription: Debouncing is essential for buttons, limit switches, and relay contacts in embedded systems.

entries.name: periodic tick scheduler
entries.description: Run periodic jobs from a millisecond tick without blocking delays.
entries.longDescription: A non-blocking periodic scheduler is often cleaner than stacking many delay calls in the main loop.

entries.name: GPIO output set clear
entries.description: Update one GPIO output using a hardware abstraction layer.
entries.longDescription: A wrapper like this keeps GPIO access explicit and easier to mock during tests.

entries.name: I2C register read
entries.description: Read a register from an I2C peripheral.
entries.longDescription: A compact helper for sensors, GPIO expanders, EEPROMs, and other small I2C peripherals.

entries.name: SPI transfer
entries.description: Exchange one full-duplex SPI frame.
entries.longDescription: This is a common baseline for reading registers from ADCs, IMUs, encoders, and other SPI devices.

entries.name: PWM duty update
entries.description: Set a PWM duty cycle from 0.0 to 1.0.
entries.longDescription: Very useful for dimming, motor speed commands, and actuator control.

entries.name: ADC moving average
entries.description: Smooth noisy ADC samples with a fixed-size moving average.
entries.longDescription: A moving average is a simple first step for stabilizing sensors and analog measurements.

entries.name: ring buffer from ISR
entries.description: Push UART bytes into a ring buffer from an interrupt.
entries.longDescription: Ring buffers are extremely common in bare-metal serial receivers because they decouple ISR speed from parser speed.

entries.name: consumer read from ring buffer
entries.description: Drain a ring buffer safely from the main loop or a task.
entries.longDescription: Keep the ISR short, then parse bytes later in a task or cooperative loop.

entries.name: FreeRTOS task skeleton
entries.description: Create a periodic FreeRTOS worker task.
entries.longDescription: A lightweight periodic task is a common starting point for embedded RTOS applications.

entries.name: finite state machine
entries.description: Drive a peripheral or workflow with explicit states.
entries.longDescription: State machines are often the clearest way to organize embedded control logic.

entries.name: libgpiod output line
entries.description: Request one GPIO line as an output and toggle it.
entries.longDescription: libgpiod is a practical Linux-side approach for modern GPIO control on Raspberry Pi and other SBCs.

entries.name: libgpiod edge wait
entries.description: Wait for a falling edge on an input GPIO.
entries.longDescription: Useful for buttons, sensors, tachometers, and external sync signals on Linux-based boards.

entries.name: I2C /dev/i2c-1 read register
entries.description: Talk to an I2C peripheral through the Linux i2c-dev interface.
entries.longDescription: A good starting point for sensors, ADCs, EEPROMs, and small interface chips on Raspberry Pi.

entries.name: spidev transfer
entries.description: Exchange a frame over SPI with /dev/spidev.
entries.longDescription: Useful for displays, ADCs, IMUs, motor drivers, and other SPI peripherals.

entries.name: PWM sysfs write
entries.description: Export and configure a PWM channel through sysfs.
entries.longDescription: A quick baseline for servo pulses or low-rate PWM control when exposed through Linux sysfs.

entries.name: UART termios on /dev/ttyAMA0
entries.description: Open the Pi UART and configure raw mode.
entries.longDescription: Useful when a Raspberry Pi acts as the Linux-side brain talking to an MCU or external controller over UART.

entries.name: multithreaded GPIO watchdog
entries.description: Poll a GPIO state in a worker thread and notify the main loop.
entries.longDescription: A worker thread is often enough on Linux-side embedded tools when the timing is not strictly hard real time.

entries.name: frame camera to command bridge
entries.description: Combine GPIO or serial control with a higher-level camera loop on the Pi.
entries.longDescription: This is a natural pattern when Raspberry Pi handles higher-level perception and delegates actuation to another board.

entries.name: setup + loop skeleton
entries.description: Minimal Arduino sketch with one LED output.
entries.longDescription: A very small baseline to validate a board, a toolchain, or a first hardware connection.

entries.name: non-blocking millis timer
entries.description: Trigger a periodic action without using delay().
entries.longDescription: millis()-based scheduling is the standard pattern once a sketch must do several things at once.

entries.name: button debounce
entries.description: Debounce a push button in the main loop.
entries.longDescription: A software debounce is often enough for user inputs and avoids false multiple triggers.

entries.name: analog read to PWM
entries.description: Map an analog input to a PWM output.
entries.longDescription: Classic for dimming, speed control demos, and bench interaction tools.

entries.name: serial command parser
entries.description: Parse line-oriented serial commands from the Arduino Serial monitor or a host PC.
entries.longDescription: A very convenient pattern when the Arduino is controlled from a PC, Raspberry Pi, or test bench script.

entries.name: attachInterrupt event flag
entries.description: Capture a pulse or button edge in an interrupt.
entries.longDescription: Keep the ISR tiny, then do heavier work later inside the main loop.

entries.name: Wire I2C sensor read
entries.description: Read one register with the Arduino Wire library.
entries.longDescription: Useful for many sensors and I2C expansion devices in Arduino projects.

entries.name: SPI peripheral transfer
entries.description: Exchange bytes with an SPI peripheral.
entries.longDescription: A compact and reusable baseline for SPI sensors, displays, and converters.

entries.name: class-based device wrapper
entries.description: Encapsulate one peripheral or subsystem in a small C++ class.
entries.longDescription: Arduino sketches stay easier to grow when devices are wrapped in small classes instead of global state everywhere.

entries.name: finite state machine sketch
entries.description: Organize sketch behavior with explicit states.
entries.longDescription: This pattern scales very well for embedded robotics and sequential control logic.

opencv_robotics_example.label: OpenCV camera and robotics example pack

entries.name: camera capture + overlay
entries.description: Capture frames and draw a crosshair overlay.
entries.longDescription: A compact base for robotics UIs, alignment tools, and vision-assisted control loops.

entries.name: HSV target mask
entries.description: Extract a colored target and compute its center.
entries.longDescription: A standard building block for color-based object tracking and simple target following.

entries.name: distance estimate from bounding box
entries.description: Estimate distance from known object width and pixel width.
entries.longDescription: Common in quick monocular estimation pipelines when the target size is known in advance.

entries.name: vision decision to command
entries.description: Translate vision offsets into simple left/right/forward commands.
entries.longDescription: A useful skeleton for proof-of-concept robotic steering driven by image-space error.

entries.name: camera reopen watchdog
entries.description: Try to reopen the camera if frame capture fails.
entries.longDescription: Very useful on embedded systems and USB cameras where transient disconnects can happen.

entries.name: search track act state machine
entries.description: Split robot vision behavior into explicit search, track, and act phases.
entries.longDescription: State machines keep robotics loops much easier to debug than a single chain of nested if statements.

entries.name: HUD overlay with FPS and target status
entries.description: Draw a compact HUD over the live frame.
entries.longDescription: A HUD is practical for demo modes, recorded videos, and operator supervision tools.

entries.name: steering command with deadband
entries.description: Turn pixel error into a bounded steering command with a deadband.
entries.longDescription: Adding a deadband keeps the robot from oscillating when the target is already near the image center.

win32_hooks_example.label: Win32 hooks and input example pack

entries.name: low-level keyboard hook
entries.description: Capture global keyboard activity with SetWindowsHookEx.
entries.longDescription: Useful for hotkeys, diagnostics overlays, and low-level input monitoring on Windows.

entries.name: register global hotkey
entries.description: Register a system-wide hotkey in a message loop.
entries.longDescription: A simpler alternative to hooks when a single hotkey is enough.

entries.name: mouse capture overlay
entries.description: Track the cursor and repaint an overlay window.
entries.longDescription: Useful for helper overlays, selection tools, and quick inspection utilities.

entries.name: raw input keyboard registration
entries.description: Receive keyboard input through WM_INPUT even without a traditional control focus.
entries.longDescription: Raw input is useful when building low-level tools that must observe device input reliably.

entries.name: click-through overlay window
entries.description: Create a transparent overlay that does not block mouse clicks.
entries.longDescription: Very useful for diagnostics overlays, crosshairs, HUDs, and assistive annotation tools.

entries.name: shortcut dispatcher
entries.description: Centralize keyboard shortcut actions in a small dispatch map.
entries.longDescription: A dispatch map stays cleaner than a long chain of if statements when tools expose many shortcuts.

entries.name: length-prefixed frame
entries.description: Build a frame with command, length, payload, and checksum.
entries.longDescription: A practical baseline for custom UART protocols with explicit payload size and integrity checks.

entries.name: line-oriented command parsing
entries.description: Parse ASCII UART commands terminated by newline.
entries.longDescription: Useful when readability and manual bench testing matter more than binary compactness.

entries.name: ACK / NACK transaction
entries.description: Retry a command until ACK arrives or the retry budget is exhausted.
entries.longDescription: A common robustness pattern for embedded links and noisy serial channels.

entries.name: state machine parser
entries.description: Parse a framed UART stream byte by byte.
entries.longDescription: State machines are often the cleanest way to parse continuous UART streams safely.

entries.name: CRC16 frame validation
entries.description: Append and validate a CRC16 on binary UART frames.
entries.longDescription: CRC16 is extremely common for field buses, device protocols, and longer binary frames.

entries.name: command dispatch table
entries.description: Route decoded command identifiers to dedicated handlers.
entries.longDescription: Dispatch tables scale nicely when the protocol exposes many commands or frame types.

entries.name: resynchronization after framing error
entries.description: Drop bytes until a new frame delimiter is found after corruption.
entries.longDescription: Resynchronization logic matters a lot on noisy links and during device resets.

instrumentation_example.label: Test bench and instrumentation example pack

entries.name: test step with verdict
entries.description: Run a step, log the result, and accumulate a verdict.
entries.longDescription: A practical skeleton for structured bench sequences and step-by-step reporting.

entries.name: CSV measurement log
entries.description: Append timestamped measurements to a CSV log.
entries.longDescription: Useful for production traces, debug campaigns, and later data analysis.

entries.name: SCPI command helper
entries.description: Write a command and read back a measurement from an instrument.
entries.longDescription: A compact pattern when controlling lab instruments and measurement hardware through SCPI.

entries.name: poll until stable measurement
entries.description: Wait until a value stays stable inside a tolerance band.
entries.longDescription: Very useful when devices need settling time before taking a final measurement.

entries.name: measurement limit check
entries.description: Evaluate a measurement against low/high tolerance limits.
entries.longDescription: Tolerance checks are the heart of many automated functional test benches.

entries.name: sequenced bench state machine
entries.description: Drive a bench sequence through setup, measure, verdict, and cleanup phases.
entries.longDescription: State machines make long automated test sequences easier to maintain and safer to extend.

entries.name: step timeout guard
entries.description: Abort a test step when it exceeds its allowed duration.
entries.longDescription: Timeout guards are essential when talking to instruments, fixtures, or boards that can stop responding.

entries.name: structured result summary
entries.description: Aggregate named step results before writing a final report.
entries.longDescription: Structured step results are useful for UIs, logs, CSV exports, and post-run diagnostics.

entries.name: CVICALLBACK
entries.description: CVI callback specifier.
entries.insertText: CVICALLBACK
entries.longDescription: Used by LabWindows/CVI for callback signatures such as panel, timer, and control callbacks.

entries.name: CVIFUNC
entries.description: CVI exported function specifier.
entries.insertText: CVIFUNC
entries.longDescription: Commonly used in CVI headers to mark externally visible functions.

entries.name: CVI callback skeleton
entries.description: Typical CVI callback function.
entries.longDescription: Typical event handler pattern for panels and controls in LabWindows/CVI.

entries.name: LoadPanel pattern
entries.description: Typical LoadPanel / DisplayPanel skeleton.
entries.longDescription: Minimal skeleton for loading a UIR file and starting the CVI UI loop.

entries.name: SetCtrlVal / GetCtrlVal pattern
entries.description: Read and write CVI control values.
entries.longDescription: One of the most common patterns when wiring UI controls to internal logic.
